Possession offers no repeated saving throw once it has taken hold. Fact: the ghost, an undead, has already possessed your fighter, and you cast protection from evil and good on him. Conclusion: the spell does not end the possession. Its 'can't be possessed' benefit is preventive, and its text for an already-possessed target grants only advantage on new saves, which this possession does not provide. It is not one of the listed ending conditions. The ruling turns on the phrase 'an effect like the dispel evil and good spell'.
